model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to 10³. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 40 to 65, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% ACC at co-occurrence number 0 and rises slightly to around 44% at 10³. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at about 44% and increases to approximately 56% at 10³. The FT method (blue line with triangular markers) starts at roughly 40% and reaches about 47% at 10³. The IKE method (red line with triangular markers) begins at approximately 43% and rises to about 49% at 10³. The ROME method (green line with square markers) starts at about 51% and shows the steepest increase, reaching approximately 66% at 10³. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the entire range.
